facts.statement: Muzquizopteryx lived during the early Coniacian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Coahuila, Mexico.
facts.quote: Muzquizopteryx is a genus of nyctosaurid pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous period (early Coniacian stage) of what is now Coahuila, Mexico.

facts.statement: A worker named José Martínez Vásquez uncovered the first skeleton of Muzquizopteryx in the 1990s at the El Rosario chalk quarry.
facts.quote: In the 1990s, José Martínez Vásquez, a worker at the chalk quarry of El Rosario, uncovered a skeleton of a pterosaur.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was acquired by the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México after its scientific value was recognized in 2002.
facts.quote: After its unique scientific value had been recognized in 2002, the specimen was acquired by the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México.

facts.statement: The species Muzquizopteryx coahuilensis was formally named and described in 2006 by Eberhard Frey, Marie-Céline Buchy, Wolfgang Stinnesbeck, Arturo González-González, and Alfredo di Stefano.
facts.quote: In 2006, the type species Muzquizopteryx coahuilensis was named and described by Eberhard Frey, Marie-Céline Buchy, Wolfgang Stinnesbeck, Arturo González-González and Alfredo di Stefano.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, UNAM IGM 8621, was found in early Coniacian-aged rocks at the El Rosario site.
facts.quote: Muzquizopteryx is based on holotype UNAM IGM 8621, found in the El Rosario layers, early Coniacian-aged rocks.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton includes soft tissue remains, specifically long fossilized tendons running along both sides of the lower arms.
facts.quote: It consists of a nearly complete, articulated skeleton that includes soft tissue remains, among them long fossilised tendons along both sides of both lower arms.

facts.statement: A second specimen, MUDE CPC-494, was reported in 2012 after being uncovered by a quarry worker and sold to a private collector.
facts.quote: In 2012, a second specimen was reported, MUDE CPC-494, again uncovered by a quarry worker, perhaps at the same site, and sold to a private collector.

facts.statement: Muzquizopteryx was relatively small for a pterodactyloid, with a wingspan of around 2 meters.
facts.quote: Muzquizopteryx was relatively small for a pterodactyloid pterosaur, with a wingspan of around 2 m.

facts.statement: The arms were very robust, featuring a large hatchet-shaped deltopectoral crest on the humerus that indicates strong wing musculature.
facts.quote: The arms were very robust with the humerus featuring a large hatchet-shaped deltopectoral crest, indicating a strong wing musculature.

facts.statement: The pteroid bone was long and pointed toward the neck, supporting the flight membrane.
facts.quote: The pteroid bone was long and pointed towards the neck, supporting a flight membrane.

facts.statement: The original describers assigned Muzquizopteryx to the family Nyctosauridae.
facts.quote: Muzquizopteryx was by its describers assigned to the Nyctosauridae.

facts.statement: Some classifications might consider Muzquizopteryx a member of the Pteranodontidae because Nyctosaurus is sometimes included in that group.
facts.quote: As Nyctosaurus is sometimes included with the Pteranodontidae, Muzquizopteryx too might be considered a member of that group under some classifications.

facts.statement: Until 2006, Muzquizopteryx was considered the smallest adult Late Cretaceous pterosaur discovered.
facts.quote: It would then be the oldest known member of the group and the smallest known; indeed the smallest adult Late Cretaceous pterosaur discovered until 2006.

facts.statement: Muzquizopteryx lived between 93.9 and 85.7 million years ago, spanning the Turonian to Coniacian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The second specimen consists of the right upper wing of a subadult individual measuring about 81% of the holotype's length.
rejected.quote: It consists of the right upper wing of a subadult individual, with about 81% of the length of the holotype.
